nt: In keeping with what is usual for his language and culture, the author uses **went up** to mark travel for change in elevation. If this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language, you can shorten it. See the Introduction to Deuteronomy for a discussion of the phrase “went up.” Alternate translation: [Then Moses went]

Here, **against the face of** represents being in front of or across from Jericho. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [across from] or [overlooking]

x.ASV: And Jehovah said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
x.Darby: And Jehovah said unto him, This is the land that I swore unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, Unto thy seed will I give it: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
x.KJV: And the Lord said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
x.YLT: And Jehovah saith unto him, `This is the land which I have sworn to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, To thy seed I give it; I have caused thee to see with thine eyes, and thither thou dost not pass over.'

nt: Here Moses is speaking as if the Israelites’ offspring were **seed**. See the Introduction to Deuteronomy for a discussion of this use of the term “seed.” Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [offspring] or [future generations]

Here the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

Yahweh is using one part of a person, his **eyes**, to mean all of him in the act of seeing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that you have seen it with your own eyes]

x.ASV: So Moses the servant of Jehovah died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of Jehovah.
x.Darby: And Moses the servant of Jehovah died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of Jehovah.
x.KJV: So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.
x.YLT: And Moses, servant of the Lord, dieth there, in the land of Moab, according to the command of Jehovah;

nt: The author is using one part of Yahweh, his **mouth**, to represent Yahweh himself in the act of speaking or commanding. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the command of Yahweh] or [what Yahweh commanded]

x.ASV: And he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab over against Beth-peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
x.Darby: And he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-Peor; and no man knows his sepulchre to this day.
x.KJV: And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth–peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
x.YLT: and He burieth him in a valley in the land of Moab, over-against Beth-Peor, and no man hath known his burying place unto this day.

nt: The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh, and the pronoun **him** refers to Moses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh buried Moses]
See how you translated this name in [Deuteronomy 3:29](../03/29.md).
See how you translated the similar phrase “until this day” in [2:22](../02/22.md). Alternate translation: [right up to this time]

The author assumes that readers will know that **to this day** refers to the time when this book was written, not to the time when Moses died. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to the time when this account was written]

x.ASV: And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
x.Darby: And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
x.KJV: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
x.YLT: And Moses is a son of a hundred and twenty years when he dieth; his eye hath not become dim, nor hath his moisture fled.

nt: The author is using **a son of 120 years** as a common expression of the culture to indicate Moses’s age. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [had lived 120 years]

The author is speaking of Moses’s eyesight as if his **eye** were something that could become **dim**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his eyesight was still strong] or [he still had good eyesight]

The author is speaking of **vigor** as if it were a living thing that could flee. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his vigor was not gone] or [his strength had not left him]

x.ASV: And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping in the mourning for Moses were ended.
x.Darby: And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; and the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.
x.KJV: And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.
x.YLT: And the sons of Israel bewail Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; and the days of weeping and mourning for Moses are completed.

x.ASV: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as Jehovah commanded Moses.
x.Darby: And Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him; and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as Jehovah had commanded Moses.
x.KJV: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
x.YLT: And Joshua son of Nun is full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him, and the sons of Israel hearken unto him, and do as Jehovah commanded Moses.

nt: The author is speaking of Joshua as if he were a container and **the spirit of wisdom** were a substance that could fill that container. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Joshua … had great wisdom] or [And Joshua … was very wise]

The author is using the possessive form to describe a **spirit** that is characterized by **wisdom**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [wisdom] or [a spirit that gave him wisdom] or [a wise spirit]

Moses’ **laying his hands on** Joshua was a symbolic action by which Moses showed that he was transferring authority to Joshua. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [had laid his hands on him to commission him as leader] or [had laid his hands on him to give him authority]

Here, **sons** means “descendants.” Moses is identifying the Israelites as descendants of their ancestor Jacob, who was also known as **Israel**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

Here the word **listen** means to intentionally hear and obey. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. See the discussion about this in the Introduction to Deuteronomy for further information. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Israel were obedient to him]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh had commanded Moses to command the Israelites]

x.ASV: And there hath not arisen a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom Jehovah knew face to face,
x.Darby: And there arose no prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom Jehovah had known face to face;
x.KJV: And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
x.YLT: And there hath not arisen a prophet any more in Israel like Moses, whom Jehovah hath known face unto face,

nt: The author is speaking of a prophet appearing or beginning to function as if he were **arisen**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And a prophet like Moses has not appeared] or [And a prophet like Moses has not come forward]

The author is using **face to face** as a common expression of his culture to mean “personally” or “directly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [directly]

x.ASV: in all the signs and the wonders, which Jehovah sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,
x.Darby: according to all the signs and wonders that Jehovah had sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land;
x.KJV: In all the signs and the wonders, which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,
x.YLT: in reference to all the signs and the wonders which Jehovah sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,

nt: The terms **signs** and **wonders** mean similar things. The author is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the miraculous signs]

x.ASV: and in all the mighty hand, and in all the great terror, which Moses wrought in the sight of all Israel.
x.Darby: and according to all that mighty hand; and according to all the great terribleness that Moses had wrought in the sight of all Israel.
x.KJV: And in all that mighty hand, and in all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.
x.YLT: and in reference to all the strong hand, and to all the great fear which Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.

nt: Here the word **hand** represents God’s power. See how you translated the similar phrase “a mighty hand” in [4:34](../04/34.md). Alternate translation: [the mighty power]

Here, **before the eyes** represents sight or witnessing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the sight] or [in the presence]
